title: Labeled ordinary towers and synchronized Zariski resolution data
statement:
Fix a totally ordered set $L$. For a reduced finite-type rational resolution input $S$ [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], say $S$ is embeddable if it is isomorphic over $\mathbf Q$ to the reduced member of an embedded resolution pair [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]; the embedding is not chosen. A labeled ordinary tower on a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] is an ordinary blowup tower [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule] with an increasing embedding of its stage index set into $L$. A labeled contracted comparison over $h:Y\to X$ is an ordinary contracted pullback comparison with equal labels at retained stages. A labeled uncontracted cartesian comparison is an uncontracted ordinary tower cartesian map [def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map] preserving every label.

For rational inputs $S,T$, a finite affine cover with total space $T$ and map $q:T\to S$ consists of finitely many affine opens $U_a\subset S$, component maps $U_a\to T$ making $T$ their coproduct [def-galois-finite-coproduct], whose composites with $q$ are the open inclusions, and whose opens cover $S$; $q$ is over $\mathbf Q$. The finite family may be empty. A labeled tower over $S$ is a resolution if its underlying tower is a regular resolution [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], its ideal modules are coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and all its levels with their composite maps to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ are of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For an uncontracted comparison, say it descends ideals if at each stage its target ideal is the unique quasi-coherent ideal whose extension equals the source ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal].

An ordinary Zariski resolution rule $A$ assigns a labeled regular ordinary resolution tower with coherent center ideals to each embeddable input, assigns a label-preserving contracted comparison to every open immersion over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-open-immersion] between these inputs, and has length zero on empty inputs. These comparisons use the full center ideals and delete exactly unit ideals, as in [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]. A tower $B$ over $S$ is an affine descent of $A$ if some finite affine cover $T\to S$ has embeddable total input and an uncontracted labeled cartesian comparison from $A(T)$ to $B$. It is a synchronized descent if every finite affine cover has such an embeddable total input and a unique such comparison descending ideals. Say $A$ has padded overlaps if for any such cover and any affine embeddable input $W$, any three open immersions $W\to T$ over the same open immersion $W\to S$ have a common labeled ordinary cartesian pullback tower $P$, together with a labeled contracted comparison from $A(W)$ to $P$ over the identity of $W$. Thus the same full tower, including unit-ideal stages, is used on triple overlaps. These are definitions of data and predicates only; no existence of a rule or of descent is asserted. For three uncontracted labeled comparisons over the identity, the composite condition means that the composite of the first two level maps equals the third level map at every stage, with the equal-length index transports.
